text:
Lena: hey hi team, first day debugging my dev setup — having trouble getting asdf to manage node/python on my M1 mac. followed the quickstart but `node -v` still shows system node. also VSCode doesn't pick up my virtualenvs. any quick checklist?
Marcus: welcome! :tada: common causes — PATH ordering and shims. does `which asdf` return ~/.asdf/bin/asdf?
Lena: `which asdf` returns /opt/homebrew/bin/asdf. i installed via brew because README suggested it. i added `\.` $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh` to zshrc, but `asdf list` is empty even after `asdf plugin-add nodejs` and `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0`
Marcus: when installed via brew we usually source the asdf script from the brew prefix. try adding to ~/.zshrc:
```
# asdf
. /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/libexec/asdf.sh
. /opt/homebrew/opt/asdf/etc/bash_completion.d/asdf.bash
```
then open a new shell and run `asdf reshim` and `asdf global nodejs 18.16.0`. that should make `node -v` point to the asdf shim.
Sasha: VSCode needs the shell integration for the integrated terminal to pick up asdf shims. in settings set `terminal.integrated.inheritEnv` true (usually default). also install the Python extension and set `python.pythonPath` to the asdf shim path or use the interpreter selector 
Kevin: quick note on python virtualenvs — after `asdf install python 3.11.4` run `python -m venv .venv` in your project and select `.venv/bin/python` in VSCode. if permissions error, run `brew reinstall openssl` and then `asdf install` again.
Lena: thanks. separate q: my ssh key isn't auto-loading so git pulls prompt for password on the code repo. i ran `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` but still asks for passphrase when pushing.
Marcus: on newer macs the keychain flag was `--apple-use-keychain` with newer ssh-add. try `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` then `git config --global core.sshCommand "ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -o IdentitiesOnly=yes"` if needed. also confirm your public key is in GitHub and in our internal git server.
Kevin: and install git-lfs: `brew install git-lfs && git lfs install`. if you cloned a repo before installing, run `git lfs pull` in the repo root. also run `gh auth login` if you use GitHub CLI.
Lena: got it — env vars question: our quickstart mentions REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ENV but i don't want to commit those. what's the recommended pattern?
Sasha: use a `.env.local` (gitignored) at project root and add a `.env.example` with placeholder keys. for secrets we use 1Password — you can run `op item get "redwood/dev/redwood-api" --fields label=password` via 1p CLI. add scripting to `scripts/bootstrap` to create `.env.local` from template.
Marcus: also our dotfiles repo has a `dev-setup` script that symlinks ssh/config and .gitconfig and sets `~/.local/bin` into PATH. check `https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles` (internal) — if you need access ping infra.
InfraBot: Welcome Lena! I created a ticket for infra to grant you repo access: #12345. JetBrains license assigned.
Lena: perfect, thanks everyone. i'll try the sourcing changes and report back. one last: any VSCode extensions worth preinstalling?
Marcus: Remote - Containers, Python, ESLint, Prettier, GitLens, Docker, Redshift? (jk) :smile:
Kevin: and the Redwood snippets extension (internal) if you can install from the marketplace.
Lena: awesome — i'll loop back if anything else blocks. merci :)
